Releasing MixOS

The accepted nightly release decision replaces the weekly whole-system cut. The 04:00 gold job builds and gates one exact source commit on CBC, installs it and accepts the desks. Only then does the private hub release job package that snapshot. A publishing failure leaves accepted gold installed. Manual nightly runs accept --no-release.

Each binary in tools/release_packages.mx and each Mix component with scripts or units has its own release line. The same contract lists server and desktop membership: packages for binaries, scripts for Mix services. Mix services are also discovered from the component index identity files. Bundles release when any member's inputs change. First run publishes all lines.

Tags are <name>-v<version>-<YYYYMMDD>, titles <name> <version> (YYYY-MM-DD). The version comes from the package (resolving workspace inheritance), the Mix component identity, or the language version printed by the gold Mix binary. Bundles use the workspace version. Existing tags and releases are never replaced. Only mixos-server requests GitHub Latest; all other lines use --latest=false.

Package already-built bytes

Run the packager from a clean throwaway checkout at the gold source commit:

mix tools/package.mix --component term --commit FULL_SHA --bin-dir /path/to/gold/bin --out /tmp/term-assets --gold-job JOB --date YYYY-MM-DD
mix tools/package.mix --components all --commit FULL_SHA --bin-dir /path/to/gold/bin --out /tmp/component-assets
mix tools/package.mix --package server --release VERSION --commit FULL_SHA --bin-dir /path/to/gold/bin --out /tmp/server-assets

--components all makes one subdirectory per component. Bundle modes remain server, desktop, and all. Each archive has one top directory with bin/ or lib/<component>/, plus component runtime data and relocatable unit templates under share/. Mix also ships a bare executable for bootstrap. SHA256SUMS.txt covers the assets and release.manifest.mx; the manifest records source, job, date, version, binary version lines and asset hashes. Highest required GLIBC_ symbol versions are informational. Packaging uses the current Arch Linux glibc; there is no glibc floor refusal. Cross-build compatibility is deferred. The old pinned libinput bundle is optional when explicitly requested with its source; normal gold packaging uses the host's libraries.

The hub nightly_release.mix plan [--gold-job ID] [--commit SHA] reads release history without remote writes. run --dry-run packages accepted current gold but stops before creating releases. run publishes each changed line at the exact source SHA, compares every uploaded asset's GitHub digest with local SHA256SUMS-bound bytes, and deletes a newly created release if verification fails. The first real publish is performed by the operator. GitHub never builds Rust.

tools/release_closure.mix statically parses Cargo manifests, including target and build dependencies and workspace-inherited path dependencies. Changes in that closure, Cargo.lock, workspace metadata, toolchain, packaging or layout inputs cause a release. Notes contain the commit range and path-limited oneline log. The previous source comes from that line's release manifest. A missing or invalid previous manifest fails closed.

Follow a component with releasesd

releasesd supports tag_prefix in schema-1 catalogue entries. It scans published, non-prerelease releases with pagination and chooses the newest publication in that line. An asset regex alone cannot choose a release line. For example:

{
  schema: 1,
  apps: [
    {name: "term", repo: "markc/mixos", tag_prefix: "term-v", asset: "^term-.*linux-x86_64[.]tar[.]gz$"},
    {name: "mix", repo: "markc/mixos", tag_prefix: "mix-v", asset: "^mix-.*linux-x86_64[.]tar[.]gz$"}
  ]
}

Explicit tags also work. Per-user installation verifies checksums and archive safety; it does not install system gold or restart desks. Default catalogue entries follow the two bundle prefixes. CI fetches the newest published mix-v* bare executable and verifies its checksum, falling back to the old full-system release only while no Mix release line exists.
